mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte depletion (potassium, magnesium) while captopril increases serum potassium and reduces renal perfusion, creating compounded renal dysfunction and dangerous hyperkalemia risk.
action: Monitor renal function, serum potassium, and electrolytes closely; consider temporary captopril discontinuation or dose reduction during amphotericin B therapy; ensure adequate hydration and monitor for acute kidney injury.
